newsitem.title: UK: P&O Nedlloyd takes over 2 P&O orders.
newsitem.headline: P&O Nedlloyd takes over 2 P&O orders.

text.p: P&O Nedlloyd Container Lines, the planned new joint venture between Britain's P&O and the Dutch Nedlloyd group, is to firm up orders for two large container ships that P&O already has on option, and add options for two more of the same, the companies said on Monday.
Lord Jeffrey Sterling, chairman of P&O, told a news conference "we will be taking up two options for 6,500 teu newbuildings and adding options for a further two".

Sterling did not say where the vessels are to be built but said they would be financed directly by P&O Nedlloyd, without recourse to guarantees from either of the partner companies who will each own half of the container operation.
One of the main aims of creating P&O Nedlloyd as a new company is to move responsibility for ship finance off the balance sheets of the two parents, executives said today.
Haddo Meijer, group finance director, said that in time P&O Nedlloyd would be seeking its own syndicated financing package but at first the new company would rely on the backup of its parents.
"First we have to make it work," he said, noting that he would be finance director of both Nedlloyd and P&O Nedlloyd initially.
